 Top-15 Border Battle Sunday in Charlotte
 Share 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 Mail 
 Print 
 No. 1/1 South Carolina Gamecocks (1-0) 
 vs.
 No. 12/11 North Carolina Tar Heels (0-1) 
 Nov 8, 2026 
 |
 5:30 pm 
 Charlotte, NC | Spectrum Center 
 TV: 
 ESPN 
 RADIO: 
 107.5 The Game 
 ONLINE: 
 Tickets 
 Live Stats 
 Game Notes 
 Media Availability 
 COLUMBIA, SC – No. 1/1 South Carolina heads just north of the stateline to face No. 12/11 North Carolina in the Ally Tipoff in Charlotte, NC, on Sun., Nov. 8. The second game of the doubleheader at Spectrum Center is slated to start at 5:30 p.m. on ESPN.
 Gamecock Notables 
 South Carolina is back in the Ally Tipoff for the second time in the last three seasons and has committed to the event for the next two seasons as well. The Gamecocks will face UConn in 2027 and NC State in 2028. The last of the series will be a rematch of South Carolina’s first trip to the event, which it won 71-57 on Nov. 10, 2024. 
 The Gamecocks opened the season pouring in 101 points against #20/17 Maryland (Nov. 2), marking their 10th game over the century mark since Nov. 7, 2025. It was the program’s sixth 100-point effort against a ranked opponent all-time with all six coming in the Dawn Staley era. 
 Sophomore Agot Makeer picked up right where she left off last season, pouring in a career-high 20 points against #20/17 Maryland on 8-of-10 shooting that included a perfect 4-of-4 night from 3-point range. She netted her first two 3s in the opening two minutes of the game to set the tone. 
 Senior Tessa Johnson has embraced point guard duties this season, leading the team with five assists in the season opener while still balancing her own scoring with 15 points. Between the two, she had her hands on 25.7 percent of the Gamecocks’ total offense. 
 Junior forward Joyce Edwards’ 23 points in the season opener led the offense for the 40th time in her career and have her ranked 34th in the nation in scoring average. She posted 13 points in the second quarter on 6-of-8 shooting. 
 Fifth-year forward Chloe Kitts’ ability to see the floor and direct the offense from the high post was a tremendous asset to the Gamecocks two seasons ago. It was on full display in her return to the court Monday as she tied for team-high honors with five assists, including three in the fourth quarter to teammates in the paint. 
 Fifth-year forward Ashlyn Watkins moved into the program’s all-time top 10 in career blocks, swatting away a pair in the season opener against #20/17 Maryland, reaching her 144 blocks in fewer 12 fewer games than anyone else on the list. Offensively, she scored all seven of her points in the fourth quarter to help hold off the Terrapins. 
 Freshman Jerzy Robinson made her presence felt in a high-profile season opener with 15 points and six rebounds. Steady down the stretch, her eight points in the fourth quarter included three free throws in the final 36 seconds. 
 By the Numbers
 3 – Three of South Carolina’s first four games are against top-20 opponents with all three games at neutral sites.
 5 – South Carolina led the way with five players on ESPN’s ranking of the top 50 players in college women’s basketball.
 18 – The Gamecocks’ 101 points in the season opener have them ranked 18th in the nation in scoring offense this week.
 The North Carolina Series
 The border series is tied 11-11 after the Gamecocks won the last four meetings, including three NCAA Tournament matchups. South Carolina is 5-4 against North Carolina in the Dawn Staley era with their last loss coming in the 2014 NCAA Tournament Sweet 16. The Gamecocks hold a 4-3 edge in games in which both teams are ranked.
 The two teams last met in the 2023-24 season when they played twice. Then-No. 1 South Carolina claimed a comeback victory at then-No. 24 North Carolina in the SEC/ACC Challenge on Nov. 30, 2023, and then dominated the Tar Heels later that season with an 88-41 win in Columbia in the second round of the 2024 NCAA Tournament. Then-sophomores Chloe Kitts and Ashlyn Watkins scored in double figures in both games
 Schedule Sketch
 Dawn Staley has built the program’s success by challenging her teams throughout the year to prepare for the NCAA Tournament.
 In 2026-27, South Carolina’s full 32-game schedule includes 15 games against teams ranked in the preseason polls, including six against top-10 foes – vs. #3/3 Southern Cal (11/15), vs. #2/2 UConn (11/24), at #4/4 Duke (12/3), at #6/6 Texas (1/3), at #8/9 Vanderbilt and #9/8 LSU (2/21). 
 Eight of the 15 games are against non-conference teams. Eleven of the 15 games are on the road (5) or at neutral sites (6).
 5:50
 ESPN released its first ranking of the top 50 players in college women’s basketball, and the Gamecocks led the way with five entries – all coming in the top 31. Freshmen were not eligible for this first list but can play their way onto the list later this season.
 Joyce Edwards came in at No. 6 after back-to-back All-America seasons. Tessa Johnson ranked No. 15 behind her steady improvement throughout her career. Chloe Kitts’ return from injury has her 27th on the list. Transfer Jordan Lee came in at No. 30, and Agot Makeer rounded out the group at No. 31.
 Thrice as Nice
 South Carolina is ranked eighth in the nation in 3-point field goal percentage after hitting 50.0 percent from the arc in the season opener against #20/17 Maryland (Nov. 2). Last season’s sharp-shooter, Tessa Johnson, who finished the season fourth in the nation in 3-point percentage at.448, hit 2-of-4 from long range in Paris.
 It was Agot Makeer who set the tone for the Gamecocks from 3-point range in the opener, though. The sophomore   hit a pair in the opening two minutes of the game and finished a perfect 4-of-4 to lead the nation in 3-point percentage and rank 27th in made 3s per game.
